page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs and 15 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor operating at 2.3 GHz, this x86_64 architecture server utilizes 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled to deliver 2 threads per core. The processor features a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The instance includes advanced instruction sets, notably Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512), which accelerate matrix multiplication and vector operations. In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates strong single-threaded performance, particularly in bzip3 decompression and text processing, where it ranks in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance in stress-ng and Geekbench falls into the bottom 25%, reflecting the physical core constraint of a 2-core, 4-thread layout. Memory bandwidth tests also show weaker performance, with uncached read and write speeds ranking in the bottom quartile.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4-standard-4 offers a dedicated CPU allocation suitable for workloads requiring predictable single-core execution without the overhead of shared-core environments. However, the lack of local NVMe storage and lower multi-core scaling are trade-offs to consider. It is best suited for light web serving, single-threaded text processing, basic LLM inference tasks using small models, and general-purpose utility workloads that do not demand high memory bandwidth or intensive multi-threaded database operations.
